title: the Ninefold Court Rising Revisited
premise: Xanthe Marchetti has spent his whole life as gatekeeper of the Hollow Vale, a valley where magic cannot enter, tending a door that must never open. When he discovers his name and tonight's date in a century-old prophecy, he learns the Ninefold Court beneath the mountain has claimed the soul of Tam, the foundling boy he raised as a brother, as payment for a bargain their dead parents made. Leaving the vale for the first time, Xanthe descends into the Court's glittering, cruel halls, where justice is a currency and belonging is bought with pieces of yourself. He wins Tam's soul back not by force but by invoking the Court's own ancient law of debts, unmaking his parents' bargain, and returns home having learned that family is not what you're born into but what you refuse to abandon.
about_author: Freya Okonkwo is a former archivist who grew up between Lagos and the Lake District, and her fiction braids West African trickster justice with Celtic underworld myth. She writes about gatekeepers, orphans, and the quiet heroism of people who stay.

chapters.title: The Date in the Margin
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. While cataloguing the vale's crumbling library, Xanthe finds a prophecy naming him and tonight's date: the night the Court beneath the mountain collects. Tam vanishes, leaving only a cold mark on the floor. Xanthe realizes the gate he guards is the debt's door, and opening it is the only way to follow. Emotional beat: the terror of discovering invisibility was a lie you told yourself.

chapters.title: Down Where the Lanterns Lie
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV, with interludes from Tam's. Xanthe crosses into the Ninefold Court, where nine masked nobles trade in souls and favors, and meets Wren, a half-forgotten servant who owes the Court everything. He learns his parents sold Tam's soul before he was born to buy the vale's protection. Emotional beat: vertigo of a world where kindness is a trap, and the first spark of found family with Wren.

chapters.title: The Ninth Mask
chapters.summary: Alternating Xanthe and Wren POVs. The Court puts Tam on trial for a debt he never incurred, and Xanthe, desperate, nearly accepts a bargain that would trade his own soul. Instead he uncovers the Ninth Mask—the hidden law older than the nine nobles, which says no soul may be held for a debt paid in full: his parents' lives were the payment. Climax: Xanthe invokes the law before the assembled Court, wagering everything on justice outside their rules.

chapters.title: What the Valley Keeps
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV, closing with Tam's. The Court, bound by its own oldest law, releases Tam's soul, and Wren chooses exile to leave with them. The three return through the gate, which Xanthe now understands was never meant to keep magic out—only to keep family in. He reopens the vale as a refuge for the Court's runaways. Emotional beat: belonging chosen, not inherited; a door that finally opens both ways.
